papers.title: IntBMoE: Integrating Block-Level Conditioning into Expert Composition for Full-Participation Mixture-of-Experts

summary.tldr: IntBMoE decouples expert participation, execution, and materialization by using a lightweight hypernetwork to compose all expert bases into sparse codebook blocks routed to tokens.
key_points: Decouples participation, execution, and materialization through block-conditioned expert composition and sparse block execution.
Uses a lightweight hypernetwork to merge all expert bases per layer into composed experts, maintaining full expert participation for every token.
Employs Dual-Path Residual Gating (DPRG) to couple two independently composed paths via multiplicative gating.
Restricts total materialized blocks to a fixed, small learned codebook size, maintaining low compute latency.
Deployed in production for AMap's generative recommendation system, meeting a 60ms latency budget with a 2.4% relative UVCTR improvement.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables full expert participation in MoE architectures without increasing execution compute or memory costs, making it suitable for strict real-time production latency budgets.

papers.title: CodeMidas: Scaling Agentic Coding RL Environments from Code Itself

summary.tldr: CodeMidas constructs executable RL training environments directly from source code, scaling dataset generation to 5,545 tasks without relying on external development artifacts like issues or commits.
key_points: Uses source code as the sole task-specific input, employing agents to explore codebase functionality, formulate behavioral specs, and build execution-grounded tests.
Filters candidate tasks using execution checks and repeated solution rollouts to ensure verifier reliability.
Yields a dataset of 5,545 training tasks across 3,185 open-source codebases, covering 23 programming languages and 15 technical domains.
Training MiMo-V2.5 using GRPO on these tasks yields performance gains across DeepSWE (+11.7%), ProgramBench (+17%), and Terminal-Bench v2.1 (+8.5%).
Trajectory analysis confirms that RL training increases codebase exploration and produces more diverse self-verification behaviors in the agent.
summary.why_it_matters: By relying solely on raw source code rather than scarce commit histories, CodeMidas unlocks massive open-source repositories to scale RL environment generation for coding agents.

papers.title: RecreationWorld: Scalable and Verifiable Environments for Hybrid Computer-Use Agents

summary.tldr: RecreationWorld introduces a multi-platform framework for hybrid computer-use agents to build and visually verify software from reference implementations, evaluated via the new 250-task RecreationBench.
key_points: Supports hybrid workflows combining GUI navigation, coding, and command-line interactions across Ubuntu, macOS, Windows, Android, and Web platforms.
Uses running reference applications as behavioral oracles to generate execution-grounded rewards via programmatic and visual assertions.
Evaluates performance on RecreationBench, where top-performing GPT-6 Astra achieved 58.1% overall accuracy but passed all programmatic tests on only 2.8% of tasks.
Training on generated trajectories improved out-of-distribution performance and increased rendered output verification across five benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a verifiable, multi-platform benchmark and environment suite for training agents that must seamlessly integrate graphical user interface actions with software development.

papers.title: Paint-Anything: Unified Any-Color Control for Image Generation and Editing

summary.tldr: Paint-Anything introduces a unified hex-prompt interface for image generation and editing, achieving precise 24-bit color control by leveraging object-level supervision and pure-color anchors.
key_points: Constructed the Paint-500K dataset using object grounding, perceptual color labeling, and editing-pair synthesis from real images.
Utilized pure-color anchors (exact hex-to-pixel matches) during high-noise diffusion timesteps, switching to natural images at low-noise timesteps to handle real-world lighting and shadows.
Introduced the Any Color Benchmark (ACBench), split into ACBench-T2I and ACBench-Edit, to evaluate object-level hex color fidelity.
Applied to FLUX.2-4B, improving ACBench-T2I scores by 85.3% and ACBench-Edit scores by 28.3% over the base model, while achieving top CompColor benchmark results.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables precise 24-bit hex color specification for visual design tasks without relying on specialized color representations or custom inference procedures.

papers.title: OmniVChat: Synthesizing, Benchmarking, and Training for Native Audio-Visual Dialogue

summary.tldr: OmniVChat introduces a native audio-visual dialogue task, a synthetic multi-agent data engine (OmniVChat-Studio), an evaluation benchmark (OmniVChat-Bench), and an RL framework (OmniVChat-RL) for training omni models without text preprocessing.
key_points: OmniVChat processes simultaneous direct audio and video inputs to generate text responses, eliminating separate speech recognition, external captioning, and text queries.
OmniVChat-Studio uses a multi-agent data engine to synthesize single- and multi-turn audio-visual dialogues, addressing data scarcity.
OmniVChat-Bench and OmniVChat-Bench-Human evaluate omni models across five basic dialogue ability categories.
OmniVChat-RL employs a reinforcement learning reward design targeting correctness, efficiency, and style, which improved Qwen3-Omni-Instruct model performance.
summary.why_it_matters: Direct audio-visual dialogue processing reduces system latency and computational overhead while enabling models to preserve key perceptual cues like facial expressions and surroundings.

papers.title: OmniVBench: A Benchmark and Large-Scale Dataset for Omni Reference-to-Video Generation

summary.tldr: OmniVBench and the Omni-R2V Dataset introduce a factor-grounded benchmark and a 340K-sample industrial training corpus to evaluate and train omni reference-to-video (R2V) generation models.
key_points: OmniVBench evaluates R2V generation across 7 task families and 18 fine-grained tasks covering content, motion, style, structure, narrative, and multi-reference settings.
Introduces factor-grounded evaluation using 12,172 case-specific checklist items to assess preservation, disentanglement, target binding, and instruction compliance.
Provides the Omni-R2V Dataset featuring 340,000 processed training samples derived from professional video footage using task-specific reference-target pair construction pipelines.
Benchmarking reveals significant performance gaps across task families and evaluation dimensions in both open- and closed-source R2V models.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes standardized, fine-grained evaluation metrics and provides a large-scale open dataset to address training data scarcity in multi-factor reference-to-video generation.

papers.title: GraphSkillEvo: Evolutionary Optimization of Graph-Structured Agent Skills

summary.tldr: GraphSkillEvo optimizes LLM agent performance by representing skills as directed natural-language graphs and refining them via population-based evolutionary algorithms.
key_points: Skill representation structures operational guidance into graph nodes for execution steps and directed edges for context-dependent transitions.
GraphSkillEvo uses population-based evolutionary optimization with mutation and crossover operators to explore structured skill spaces beyond standard LLM self-refinement.
Evaluations show performance improvements over the SkillOpt baseline, increasing average accuracy by 4.01% on GPT-5.4-nano and 1.76% on GPT-5.4 across five benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: Structuring instructions into graphs and applying evolutionary operators reduces procedural redundancy and constrained search spaces, enabling more effective automated skill refinement for LLM agents.

papers.title: MintAct: A Unified Visual Agent for Digital Environments

summary.tldr: MintAct is a family of vision-language models (2B, 4B, 8B) that unifies UI grounding, multi-step cross-platform navigation, and visual tool use, achieving a state-of-the-art 48.9 score on OSWorld-Verified.
key_points: Trained across 2B, 4B, and 8B parameter scales to unify UI grounding, visual tool use, and multi-step navigation on mobile, desktop, and web.
Hosts hundreds of concurrent instances across heterogeneous per-domain backends for trajectory collection and online reinforcement learning (RL).
Uses an asynchronous RL training framework to maintain explicit control over cross-domain training distributions and manage noisy environment feedback and off-policy drift.
Matches the performance of domain-specific models and sets a SOTA score of 48.9 on the OSWorld-Verified benchmark.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that a single vision-language agent can match or exceed domain-specialized models across desktop, mobile, and web environments through scalable asynchronous RL.

papers.title: When AI Reviews Train AI Reviewers: Scientific-Judgment Collapse and Mitigation

summary.tldr: Fine-tuning LLM peer reviewers on synthetic reviews causes scientific-judgment collapse, which the proposed TrustReviewer system mitigates using curated training data and paired activation steering.
key_points: Recursive training of Llama 3.1 8B on model-generated ICLR reviews compresses rating distributions and reduces same-paper and corpus-level semantic diversity.
TrustReviewer uses a single-stage training intervention on a curated corpus to prevent low-quality and semantically degenerate supervision.
TrustReviewer applies test-time paired activation steering to correct residual collapsed judgments without requiring retraining or additional human annotations.
summary.why_it_matters: It identifies and offers concrete mitigations for the degradation of automated peer-review quality caused by recursive training on AI-generated evaluations.

papers.title: Calibrating Teacher--Student Discrepancy for On-Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: Calibrated On-Policy Distillation (Cal-OPD) filters out teacher self-deviations by calibrating the teacher-student discrepancy via positive and negative privileged interventions, retaining only the true capability gap for optimization.
key_points: Standard on-policy distillation (OPD) incorrectly forces students to learn teacher-side likelihood shifts and self-deviations alongside the actual capability gap.
Privileged OPD exacerbates teacher self-deviation due to larger likelihood shifts caused by privileged information.
Cal-OPD isolates the teacher's self-deviation region using positive and negative privileged interventions, stripping it from the optimization target.
Cal-OPD retains only 52-65% of the original teacher-student discrepancy signal while consistently outperforming standard OPD across mathematical reasoning benchmarks and model scales.
summary.why_it_matters: By removing noisy teacher self-deviations, Cal-OPD achieves higher mathematical reasoning performance while training on roughly half the signal volume of standard on-policy distillation.

papers.title: TeleAntiFraud 2.0: A Refreshable, Profile-Grounded, and Audio-Based Benchmark for Telecom Fraud Detection

summary.tldr: TeleAntiFraud 2.0 is a refreshable benchmark using a Mixed-Tree Anti-Fraud Generation Pipeline and monthly frozen sets of 900 Chinese calls to evaluate audio-based telecom fraud models against hard, near-domain non-fraud negatives.
key_points: Features a monthly frozen evaluation protocol containing 900 Chinese audio calls per set (600 fraud and 300 near-domain non-fraud cases) built from real online fraud abstracts.
Uses a Mixed-Tree Anti-Fraud Generation Pipeline to create profile-grounded scenarios and generate fraud and non-fraud dialogue paths under shared contexts.
Classifier Macro-F1 scores dropped from 1.0 on unrelated negatives to 0.65-0.68 when tested against near-domain sibling negatives in text experiments.
Audio and ASR+LLM evaluations identified critical model vulnerabilities including class-prior shortcuts, prediction collapse, and snapshot sensitivity.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that conventional benchmarks overestimate telecom fraud detection accuracy by using overly distinct negative controls, establishing near-domain construction as essential for realistic model evaluation.

papers.title: DeformSmith: Physics Harness-Guided Hierarchical Generation of Deformable Assets for Robot Manipulation

summary.tldr: DeformSmith is a framework for generating interactive, physically credible deformable assets from text or a single image using hierarchical agentic construction and a shared physics-grounded harness.
key_points: Jointly generates geometry, appearance, material behavior, and physical models for deformable object simulation.
Uses a shared physics-grounded harness to progressively build, test, and refine physical properties based on contact and deformation responses.
Closes the generation loop via robot interaction feedback and replayable interaction data for training downstream manipulation tasks.
Outperforms state-of-the-art baselines including PhysGen3D, PhysGM, and PhysX-Omni in visual quality and physical plausibility.
summary.why_it_matters: It automates the creation of simulation-ready deformable 3D assets with accurate physical dynamics, advancing data synthesis for robotic manipulation.

papers.title: FRAUDSkill: Structured Frozen-Weight Skill Optimization for Audio Anti-Fraud Detection

summary.tldr: FRAUDSkill introduces a structured frozen-weight adaptation framework for audio-language models that optimizes external skill programs and route-specific policies without modifying underlying model weights.
key_points: Leaves the core audio-language model frozen while optimizing external skill programs, route-specific policies, and decision rules.
Enforces a structured decision protocol covering service-scenario identification, fraud detection, and conditional fraud-type classification.
Employs structured output control alongside validation-guided multi-path inference to enforce label space constraints.
Achieves 73.50% Macro-F1 on the TeleAntiFraud benchmark, outperforming the shared frozen-model baseline by 31.96% and reducing invalid outputs to 1.94%.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables rapid adaptation of audio anti-fraud systems to evolving fraud patterns and labeling policies without expensive model retraining.

papers.title: Refinement Is Inherently Editable: Training-Free Prompt-to-Prompt Image Editing with Generative Refinement Network

summary.tldr: RefineEdit is a training-free prompt-to-prompt image editing framework that couples edit localization with content generation by globally refining binary image codes via a Generative Refinement Network.
key_points: Initializes an editing branch from an intermediate source state to reuse the emerging layout.
Compares bit probabilities between source and edit branches, using signed probability differences to select editable positions and bits while copying unselected bits from the source.
Employs adaptive spatial freezing to limit mask expansion and finite bit locking to keep recently selected bits editable across refinement steps.
Requires no extra training, external masks, or attention control mechanisms.
Outperforms evaluated methods on PIE-Bench in background preservation (PSNR, LPIPS, MSE, SSIM) and CLIP similarity scores (whole-image and edited-region).
summary.why_it_matters: It enables precise, training-free text-guided image editing with superior background preservation without relying on spatial controls, attention tuning, or external masks.

papers.title: Learning Foresight without Explicit Trajectories for 3D Diffusion Policies

summary.tldr: Movement Trend Guidance adds implicit future foresight to 3D diffusion policies via a compact latent representation supervised by sparse future gripper states, improving task success without requiring explicit trajectory planning.
key_points: Trains a compact latent representation of interaction evolution using sparse future gripper states for supervision, requiring only current observations and historical context at inference.
Injects future-oriented conditioning via global action conditioning and a gated FiLM branch specifically at the UNet bottleneck.
Adds 3.52% additional parameters to the DP3 architecture while preserving its dense-action and receding-horizon formulation.
Outperforms base DP3 on LIBERO-40 (71.93% vs 37.08%), 50-task RoboTwin2.0 mixed training (62.8% vs 56.1%), and five real-robot tasks (72.0% vs 49.0%).
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that incorporating high-level temporal direction into diffusion policies substantially improves robotic manipulation performance without the overhead of generating explicit trajectory plans.

papers.title: Micro-Collaborative Poisoning: A Distributed Attack on RAG Systems

summary.tldr: Micro-Collaborative Poisoning splits a false target claim across multiple locally plausible documents, attacking RAG systems through the accumulation of weak adversarial signals rather than a single explicit malicious passage.
key_points: Evaluated across 108 RAG configurations by manipulating dataset, retriever architecture, top-k retrieval depth, database composition, generator model, and number of poisoned databases.
Downstream attack success relies on the co-occurrence of weak signals in the retrieved context, which is amplified by higher top-k values and multiple poisoned databases.
Mitigation occurs naturally when using stronger retrievers and increasing clean database diversity.
Document-level visibility analysis demonstrates that the attack leaves a weaker explicit poisoning signature than direct single-passage poisoning, evading isolated document inspection.
summary.why_it_matters: Conventional single-document inspection methods fail to detect these attacks because the adversarial payload is distributed across seemingly benign passages.

papers.title: On Repulsive and Attractive Teachers: Separating Correctness from Behavior in Self-Distillation

summary.tldr: A study on self-distillation reveals that attractive and repulsive teachers induce opposing behavioral shifts, and proposes contrastive self-distillation to cancel these behavioral shifts and isolate correctness-relevant signals.
key_points: Attractive self-distillation (moving toward a privileged teacher) suppresses exploratory reasoning and yields shorter, overly confident responses.
Repulsive self-distillation (moving away from a privileged teacher) increases response length, causes unstable training, and can trigger unintended switches into latent thinking modes.
Contrastive self-distillation combines attraction toward a correct-solution-conditioned teacher with repulsion from an incorrect-solution-conditioned teacher.
Isolating contrastive self-distillation without GRPO causes the shared behavioral shifts of both teachers to cancel out, leaving a stable, token-level correctness signal.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables improved reasoning performance across non-thinking, instruct-only, and thinking LLMs while preventing training instability and unwanted length or behavioral drifts.

papers.title: LogicTrack: Auditing Reasoning Trajectories of Large Language Models with Formal Logic Solvers

summary.tldr: LogicTrack is a neuro-symbolic framework that auto-formalizes LLM Chain-of-Thought reasoning steps into symbolic representations and verifies them using automated theorem provers.
key_points: Introduces Solver-Based Backtracking Reward (SBR), a step-wise scoring mechanism that measures logical soundness to guide backtracking tree search during inference.
Extends trajectory data to construct supervised fine-tuning (SFT) datasets with backtracking traces, allowing models to internalize step-wise auditing capabilities.
Addresses the issue of models reaching correct final answers via logically flawed intermediate steps.
Evaluated across 8 reasoning benchmarks using 7 different large language models.
summary.why_it_matters: By enforcing intermediate logical validity through formal solvers, LogicTrack improves the overall verifiability, accuracy, and trustworthiness of language model reasoning in high-stakes applications.

papers.title: Abstention and Noise Filtering: Two Missing Primitives of Softmax Attention

summary.tldr: A study shows value-pathway gating in softmax attention provides two distinct missing primitives: abstention via learned per-head sink logits and noise filtering via value gates, with filtering benefits dominating as models scale to 350M parameters.
key_points: Abstention (learned per-head sink logit) allows attention heads to output zero by bypassing the sum-to-one softmax constraint, while noise filtering (per-value gates) suppresses residual stream feature interference.

Abstention accounts for almost all performance gains at 10M parameters but its benefit declines with scale, whereas noise filtering benefits increase with scale and drive most gains at 350M parameters.
Models combining both abstention and noise filtering achieved the lowest validation loss across all tested scales (10M to 350M parameters).
Controlled interference experiments confirm value gates remove superposed feature noise, though each tested gate variant exhibits a distinct blind spot.
Adding both primitives requires negligible extra parameters and maintains compatibility with standard KV-caching.
summary.why_it_matters: Combining sink logits and value gates fixes fundamental limits of softmax attention to improve scaling performance without overhead or breaking KV-cache compatibility.

papers.title: ExpBoN: Exponential-Noise Best-of-$n$ for Efficient Test-Time LLM Alignment

summary.tldr: ExpBoN introduces an exponential-noise report-noisy-max mechanism for soft Best-of-n sampling, which integrates into guided speculative inference (ExpGSI) to lower test-time compute costs during LLM alignment.
key_points: ExpBoN uses an exponential-noise report-noisy-max mechanism that admits an exact finite-n decomposition.
The method achieves exponentially fast convergence in total variation, expected reward, and forward/reverse KL divergence.
ExpBoN is combined with guided speculative inference to create ExpGSI for reward-guided LLM alignment.

Empirical evaluations on MATH500, MMLU-STEM, and Minerva Math show ExpGSI cuts estimated computation by 14%-39% for Qwen2.5-Math models and up to 45% at n=16 for Qwen3 models while maintaining accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: ExpGSI enables significantly more efficient inference-time alignment of large language models by drastically reducing the computational overhead of Best-of-n sampling without sacrificing accuracy.

papers.title: RheoSampling: Resolving the One-Hot Dilemma in Stochastic Dynamic-Tree Speculative Decoding

summary.tldr: RheoSampling decouples dynamic-tree construction from token verification by using proxy probabilities for stochastic tree expansion, resolving acceptance rate drops in non-zero temperature speculative decoding while maintaining losslessness.
key_points: Identifies that dynamic-tree methods (e.g., EAGLE-3) collapse draft distributions to one-hot probabilities under stochastic decoding (T>0) because the same distribution is used for tree construction and verification.
Decouples operations by assigning sampled draft tokens a proxy probability for context-aware top-K tree expansion/pruning while retaining true sampling probabilities for verification.
Proves mathematical losslessness using an equivalence-class analysis to compress the stochastic tree space into tractable classes.
Integrates an Optimal Transport (OT)-based verification strategy and a sparse draft mechanism to ensure efficient target model execution.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables context-aware dynamic-tree speculative decoding to maintain high acceptance rates and speedups during stochastic sampling without sacrificing output distribution accuracy.

papers.title: SpecQuant: Speculative Decoding with Multi-Parent Quantization for Adaptive LLM Inference

summary.tldr: SpecQuant is a training-free framework combining speculative decoding with multi-parent quantization, dynamically routing queries between INT4, FP8, and FP16 variants derived from a single base model based on task complexity.
key_points: Derives multiple quantized weight variants (INT4, FP8, FP16) from a shared base model to eliminate separate draft models and compatibility issues.
Dynamically routes simple or factual tasks to lightweight variants and complex reasoning or long-context tasks to full-precision variants.
Evaluated on Qwen2.5-based models using MMLU, AlpacaEval, and GSM8K benchmarks.
Achieves a 35-43% inference speedup while maintaining accuracy within 2% of the original model.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables high-speed, adaptive LLM inference on resource-constrained consumer hardware without requiring model retraining, dedicated draft models, or per-architecture tuning.

papers.title: Beyond Gaussian Worlds: Latent Geometry Matters for JEPAs

summary.tldr: New theoretical analysis shows that JEPAs matching spherical target distributions achieve exact linear (orthogonal) recovery, disproving the claim that isotropic Gaussians are uniquely recoverable.
key_points: Extends JEPA representation collapse theoretical analysis from Euclidean spaces to latent variables on embedded Riemannian manifolds.
Proves that matching representations to a uniform spherical target guarantees latent state recovery up to an orthogonal transformation.
Derives an approximate-recovery bound that is strictly tighter for spherical latent spaces than for Gaussian latent spaces.

Demonstrates empirically on Gaussian, spherical, and toroidal (including high-dimensional Clifford-torus) spaces that geometrically compatible targets improve linear recovery, whereas mismatched targets distort latent structure.
summary.why_it_matters: Selecting a target distribution that matches the underlying manifold geometry of the latent space prevents representation distortion and improves feature recovery in self-supervised JEPAs.

papers.title: Trading Depth for Time in Recurrent Transformers

summary.tldr: Latent Recurrent Transformers (LRTs) trade physical depth for temporal steps by inserting latent thought tokens, achieving near-equivalent performance with 48% fewer parameters.
key_points: Interleaves latent thought tokens between consecutive vocabulary tokens to pass hidden states through an L-layer backbone twice per token, executing 2L Transformer blocks total.
Evaluated on 16- and 20-layer mixture-of-experts NanoChat backbones, comparing an L-layer model using one thought token against a 2L-layer model without thought tokens.
One thought token brings the L-layer model within 0.006 and 0.004 bits per byte of the 2L-layer baseline, recovering 67% and 81% of the performance gains.
Demonstrates that temporal recurrence can substitute for physical depth to improve parameter efficiency in recurrent Transformers.
summary.why_it_matters: Using temporal recurrence with latent tokens enables smaller, more parameter-efficient models to achieve language modeling performance comparable to significantly deeper backbones.

papers.title: Detecting Hallucination in LLMs: Tracing the Topological Signatures of Impaired Context Sharing

summary.tldr: A single-pass method detects LLM hallucinations by using Forman-Ricci curvature to trace topological signatures of impaired context sharing in attention graphs.
key_points: Analyzes Forman-Ricci curvature on attention graphs to identify structural information bottlenecks and over-squashing.
Captures semi-local and global information-flow characteristics of attention heads to differentiate hallucinated responses.
Identifies that hallucinated outputs correlate with self-attention over-reliance, diffused context retrieval, and information bottlenecks, particularly in the final transformer layer.
Outperforms existing attention-based and multi-response baselines across two benchmarks without requiring multiple response generation passes.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables computationally efficient, single-pass hallucination detection across diverse LLM architectures without the overhead of generating multiple responses.

security.title: APort Vault: Benchmarking AI Agent Payment Authorization with the Open Agent Passport

summary.tldr: APort Vault benchmarks AI agent payment authorization using 4,371 human-written attacks across 14 models, demonstrating that a deterministic Open Agent Passport (OAP) pre-action check reduced unauthorized transfers from 140 to zero.
key_points: Evaluated 14 models across 225,964 total runs using 4,371 attacks from a live capture-the-flag event under five policy configurations.
Adding the deterministic OAP pre-action check layer reduced unauthorized payment recipient transfers from 140 (out of 76,842 model-alone runs) to 0 (out of 69,297 runs).
The OAP layer maintained utility by executing 25,370 valid payments while denying 187 of 25,640 evaluated transfer calls (148 for forbidden recipients).
Payment request rates varied drastically by policy configuration level (from 0.1% at Level 3 to 79.4% at Level 4) rather than by the underlying model.
summary.why_it_matters: Enforcing deterministic pre-action security policies via specifications like OAP eliminates unauthorized AI agent payment transfers without resorting to blunt payment refusals.

security.title: End-to-End Hard-Label Cryptanalytic Model Extraction Using Efficient Sign Recovery

summary.tldr: A new sign-recovery algorithm enables the first fully black-box, end-to-end hard-label parameter extraction of trained deep ReLU MLPs without requiring dedicated sign-recovery queries.
key_points: Eliminates dedicated queries for the sign-recovery phase, reducing overall query complexity and computational burden compared to the Eurocrypt 2025 method by Carlini et al.
Achieves higher sign-recovery accuracy on trained models than previous techniques.
Demonstrates full black-box extraction on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST models with width 16 and 4 to 6 hidden layers, achieving over 98% label agreement.
summary.why_it_matters: It proves that deep ReLU MLP model parameters can be fully stolen in a strict black-box hard-label setting where adversaries only observe final classification labels.

security.title: Watermarkable Multi-Draft Speculative Sampling via Poisson Processes

summary.tldr: A novel multi-draft speculative sampling algorithm based on Poisson processes enables unbiased, provably effective watermarking without sacrificing sampling efficiency or speculative acceptance rates.
key_points: Utilizes a Poisson process framework to achieve an exact list-coupling-without-communication scheme for multi-draft speculative sampling.
Provides a drafter invariance property that optimizes both language model sampling performance and watermark robustness.
Allows the embedding of an unbiased watermark into the generation process without degrading the speculative acceptance rate.
First multi-draft scheme to simultaneously preserve watermark strength, drafter invariance, and inference efficiency.
summary.why_it_matters: It resolves a key trade-off in LLM deployment by allowing fast inference acceleration via speculative sampling alongside reliable content provenance verification through watermarking.

security.title: CASCADE Against Jailbreaks: Combination Across Stages with Controlled Attack-Defense Evaluation

summary.tldr: CASCADE introduces a standardized decision framework to systematically evaluate and combine 15 defenses across different pipeline stages against 19 single-turn, black-box LLM jailbreak attacks.
key_points: Evaluates 15 defenses and 19 attacks within a unified threat model focusing on direct, black-box, single-turn jailbreak attempts.
Establishes a standardized attack-success-rate (ASR) formulation that controls query budgets and enforces explicit fairness rules.
Demonstrates that while no single defense is universally optimal, multi-stage defense combinations maximize safety with minimal utility loss.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides empirical guidance for building effective layered defense pipelines that mitigate LLM jailbreak risks without severely impacting model utility.

security.title: TERMon: Detecting Persistent Behavioral Threats in Edge AI via Hardware-Native Ternary Runtime Monitor

summary.tldr: TERMon is a hardware runtime monitor for Edge AI that detects behavioral anomalies using pipelined ternary pattern matching against thermometer-encoded feature fingerprints with a two-cycle latency.
key_points: Monitors inference behavior directly rather than using model re-execution or formal verification methods.
Encodes class-conditional trusted behavior as ternary patterns matching unquantized range decisions exactly.
Implemented on a PYNQ-Z2 FPGA using a pipelined architecture requiring zero block RAM (BRAM) or DSP blocks.
Successfully detects harmful weight corruptions based on behavioral impact, though out-of-distribution and adversarial inputs remain largely inseparable at strict false-positive operating points.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables real-time detection of model corruption in safety-critical edge environments with minimal FPGA resource overhead and a two-cycle latency.

security.title: CIPL: A Channel-Aware Framework for Recoverable Privacy Leakage in LLM Agents

summary.tldr: CIPL is a channel-aware framework that evaluates black-box privacy leakage in LLM agents by modeling how internal sensitive data translates into externally attacker-recoverable output.
key_points: Models target systems across six stages: sensitive source, selection, assembly, execution, observation, and extraction.
Evaluates transition from selected sensitive units to attacker-recoverable output across memory, retrieval, and tool-mediated pipelines, including a BrowserUse live-agent case study.

Demonstrates that internal storage labels do not dictate recoverability: memory targets show near-saturated leakage, retrieval-mediated leakage is often partial, and tool/live-agent leakage depends on observation surface, prompt-channel alignment, retrieval depth, and provider behavior.
Employs a stratified semantic audit to detect attacker-useful privacy disclosures that canonical exact matching metrics fail to capture.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a standardized method to quantify actual, externally recoverable privacy risks in complex LLM agents rather than relying on misleading internal storage metrics.

security.title: ServeGuard: Verifiable, Bounded-Residual Confinement of Operator-Invisible Channels Without Revealing the Certified Read Factor

summary.tldr: ServeGuard provides a zero-knowledge supply-chain primitive that proves a third-party open-weight adapter carries no hidden backdoor channels in a safety monitor's blind subspace, without revealing the adapter's certified read factor.
key_points: Payload detection in a monitor's blind subspace is unsound because benign and backdoored adapters overlap on blind-subspace statistics.
ServeGuard enforces zero-knowledge proofs for a single linear identity, leveraging the public base model to deterministically identify blind spots without exposing the certified read factor.
Serves a residual bounded by the public base model's own floor rather than a prover-chosen tolerance, paired with an admission-time typing guard to lock in adapter bytes.

Evaluated across eight checkpoints up to 7B from four families, showing monitoring budget saturation at the value-path rank for grouped-query architectures and near-zero cost for benign adaptation on a 0.5B model.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows model consumers and regulators to mathematically verify the safety of opaque third-party adapters without requiring publishers to disclose proprietary weight matrices.

security.title: HE-Guardrail: A Homomorphic Guardrail Against Jailbreak Attacks for Encrypted Large Language Model Inference

summary.tldr: HE-Guardrail is a framework that evaluates input prompts and controls output responses directly over homomorphically encrypted data to prevent jailbreak attacks during privacy-preserving LLM inference.
key_points: Identifies that Homomorphic Encryption (HE) prevents servers from inspecting prompts, leaving HE-LLM inference vulnerable to undetected adversarial and jailbreak attacks.
Proposes HE-Guardrail to execute safety checks entirely over encrypted data and homomorphically block harmful responses from returning to the client.
Instantiates and evaluates the framework using three existing guardrail mechanisms: Llama Guard, JBShield, and GradSafe.
Demonstrates that encrypted guardrails closely match plaintext decision accuracy while presenting specific security, efficiency, and utility trade-offs.
summary.why_it_matters: It resolves a fundamental conflict in privacy-preserving LLM deployment by allowing servers to enforce safety and alignment policies without compromising client data privacy.

security.title: Authorization Revocation for Long-Running AI Agents: Root-Scoped Quiescence under Delegation and Asynchronous Execution

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced a root-scoped authorization quiescence protocol that revokes long-running AI agent authority across delegated queues, callbacks, and provider operations by linearizing root cuts and issuing provider-frontier certificates.
key_points: Defines root-scoped authorization quiescence to fence old-root expansion and protected sinks while allowing exact rebind to independently sufficient alternative support.
Represents alternative and conjunctive authority as antichains of minimal sufficient root sets and composes certificates into a cutset over registered paths using exact channel-token accounting.
Formally proves post-cut issuer non-expansion, support-sound projection, compositional soundness under exact channel conservation, and crash/replay stability.
Validated via a late-effect test suite matching 17/17 registered outcomes, where cut-plus-fence executions successfully rejected scheduled late effects that cancellation-only executions accepted.
Includes an independent trace checker that verified 17/17 traces and rejected 44/44 semantic regressions.
summary.why_it_matters: Standard process cancellation or credential revocation fails to stop asynchronous, multi-provider AI agent operations, whereas this protocol provably prevents unauthorized late-execution side effects.

security.title: Origin Is All You Need: Provenance-Aware Transformers for Structural Trust-Boundary Separation

summary.tldr: Provenance-Aware Transformers eliminate indirect prompt injection by introducing architectural source boundaries using ring IDs, origin embeddings, learnable origin attention biases, and origin scales.
key_points: Indirect prompt injection vulnerability stems from standard transformers processing system instructions, user inputs, and retrieved data through an undifferentiated attention mechanism.

The proposed architecture assigns each token a ring ID to denote source origin and adds origin embeddings, a learnable origin attention bias, and a learnable origin scale to maintain provenance through normalization.
A two-stage fine-tuning pipeline trains pretrained models to execute tasks under ring-constrained origin semantics.
Evaluations demonstrate robust in-distribution and out-of-distribution resistance to indirect prompt injections while preserving base model utility.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach shifts LLM safety from brittle text-based pattern matching to explicit, architectural trust-boundary enforcement.

summary.tldr: Researchers identify Loopjacking, an agentic security vulnerability where human approval for operation A is exploited to execute a materially different operation B via representation mismatch or post-approval state substitution.
key_points: Post-approval state-substitution attacks were reproduced in seven Agno AgentOS releases (up to 3.0.9) and 12 LangGraph Agent Server compositions (up to 0.14.0).
Representation mismatch attacks were successfully executed in OpenClaw 2026.2.23, but rejected in version 2026.2.24.
OpenAI Agents SDK (0.22.0 and 0.22.2) blocked attacks by using serialized continuation to maintain per-call binding and reject mutated states.
Mitigation requires canonical approval rendering combined with exact use-time state comparison or restricting unauthorized pending-state mutation.
summary.why_it_matters: Human-in-the-loop controls fail as a final security boundary if agent frameworks do not cryptographically or statefully bind the user's specific approval to the exact downstream payload executed.

security.title: CESBench: Benchmarking Large Language Models on Cryptographic Engineering Security for IoT Devices

summary.tldr: CESBench is a new public benchmark evaluating LLMs across 380 expert-written items in six IoT cryptographic engineering security sub-domains using four task types and 572 test cases.
key_points: Benchmark evaluates six sub-domains: side-channel, fault injection, implementation, countermeasures, evaluation, and integration.
Includes four task types: 209 multiple-choice, 67 judgment, 63 scenario diagnosis, and 41 code tasks scored against 572 test cases.
Evaluated 11 open-weight and proprietary LLMs, with composite scores ranging from 54.4% to 83.6%.
Models achieved high scores in multiple-choice (up to 98.6%) and code tasks (up to 95.1%), but struggled with judgment tasks (top score of 58.8%).
While models got 88.5% of security verdicts correct, their written justifications earned only 53.4% of available rubric marks.
summary.why_it_matters: It reveals that while LLMs excel at recall and coding in cryptographic engineering, they lack reliability in justifying security verdicts critical for IoT physical attack resilience.

security.title: Conformal Privacy Auditing: Calibrated Re-identification Attacks with Statistical Guarantees

summary.tldr: Conformal Privacy Auditing (CPA) is a distribution-free calibration framework that provides finite-sample statistical guarantees and ambiguity sets for document re-identification risk against LLM-empowered adversaries.
key_points: CPA outputs a conformal ambiguity set of candidate identities guaranteed to contain the true identity with user-chosen confidence under exchangeability.
Derives an interpretable identity leakage proxy directly from the size of the conformal ambiguity set.
Supports both logit-access and sampling-only attacker models, enabling unified auditing of open-source and proprietary API-based LLMs.
Demonstrates calibrated coverage and tracks shifts in certified identifiability across varying auxiliary knowledge, LLM augmentations, and release mechanisms.
summary.why_it_matters: It offers a statistically grounded, calibrated methodology to evaluate and compare individual document re-identification risks at release time without relying on uncalibrated attack success rates.

security.title: (Don't) Trust, but (Don't) Verify: Developers' Attention to Security in AI-Generated Code

summary.tldr: A 100-participant observational study isolated how developers evaluate AI-generated C code suggestions across security and functionality dimensions before finalizing submissions.
key_points: Study isolated the code evaluation phase using four C linked-list tasks where developers cycled through five AI suggestions varying in security and functionality.
Participants selected, edited, and submitted code options while completing post-study surveys and follow-up interviews (n=23) on trust and decision-making.
Research investigated developer ability to identify vulnerabilities, evaluation cues used, and the impact of trust on code acceptance.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding how developers evaluate and trust AI-generated suggestions is crucial for designing safer AI coding assistants and preventing the deployment of vulnerable code.

security.title: Provisional Reachability: Containing Agents by Making Every Crossing Revocable

summary.tldr: A provisional reachability defense places agent crossings in escrow to cap adversary information leakage at L(r) ~ c/(er) bits per period, preventing secret assembly when paired with decay rates exceeding g/L.
key_points: Escrowing k crossings carrying c bits with independent audit probability r bounds information leakage per window to a supremum of L(r) ~ c/(er), matched in simulation to 7.7 standard errors.

Pairing escrow with a secret decay fraction mu creates an Eigen-style error threshold, guaranteeing an L-bit secret is unreachable when mu > g/L (100% secret assembly at 0.9mu* vs 0% at 2mu* over 20,000 windows).
Keying denotations hides 2.64 of 3.00 bits at chance accuracy while preserving valid Python syntax, whereas keying entry points hides only 0.10 bits.
The full defensive stack reduces total data leaks from 100,000 to 59 bits (a 1,704x reduction); caller-keyed windows restore legitimate work execution from 12% to 100% without increasing leakage.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a mathematically provable, public rate limit on information exfiltration for autonomous agents without relying on adversary deception.

summary.tldr: vLLM achieved 5,000 total tokens/s per GPU throughput and 180 generated tokens/s per user interactivity serving the Qwen3.8-2.4T model using Prompt-Decode disaggregation on a GB300 NVL72 cluster.
key_points: Evaluated on an 8K/1K workload, demonstrating the full Pareto frontier for both high-throughput and low-latency scenarios.
Qwen3.8-2.4T architecture features 92 total layers (69 GDN layers and 23 Full-Attn layers) with NVFP4 MoE blocks (92 × 512 experts) and BF16 attention layers.
Decoupled state sizing requires accounting for token-dependent Full-Attn KV cache (2 KiB per layer per token) and static per-request GDN state (4,216 KiB total per request).
Provides reproducible srt-slurm recipes and a step-by-step decision framework for tuning KV cache block allocations and concurrency limits.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes benchmark performance metrics and a reusable optimization methodology for serving trillion-parameter hybrid MoE models efficiently using disaggregated serving architectures.

infra.title: Inside Petal: Building the World’s First Petabit-Class Transoceanic Subsea Cable

summary.tldr: Meta announced Petal, a 7,000 km transatlantic subsea cable planned for 2029 that uses 2-core multi-core fiber to achieve a record 1 Pbps capacity.
key_points: Petal connects France and the US over ~7,000 km, doubling the 0.5 Pbps capacity of the 24-fiber-pair Anjana cable to achieve 1 Pbps (1,000 Tbps).
The system deploys 2-core fiber technology across 24 fiber pairs, delivering optical throughput equivalent to a 48-fiber-pair system.
The multi-core fiber maintains a standard 125 µm outer diameter, manufactured by Sumitomo Electric from preforms stretched from 20 cm wide to thousands of kilometers long.
Built in partnership with NEC, Sumitomo Electric, and Orange, the cable avoids doubling physical infrastructure, materials, and power demands to scale capacity.
summary.why_it_matters: Petal introduces multi-core fiber at scale to bypass the Shannon Limit, allowing transoceanic networks to double data throughput without increasing physical cable size or environmental footprint.
